title: Passato prossimo with avere
description: The compound past: avere + past participle; regular and irregular participles.
objectives: Form the passato prossimo with avere and use it for completed events.

blocks.title: auxiliary + past participle
blocks.text: The passato prossimo is formed with the present of *avere* (or *essere*, next lesson) + the past participle: *ho mangiato* = I ate / I have eaten.

blocks.title: With avere the participle does not change
blocks.text: With *avere* the participle normally stays in -o, whoever the subject is: *Sara ha mangiato, i bambini hanno mangiato*. The main exception is a 3rd-person direct object pronoun placed before the verb: *Le mele? Le ho mangiate.* All the agreement rules are in [[ausiliari-accordo|auxiliaries and agreement]].
Many -ere verbs, and a few others, have irregular participles. They must be learned, but they fall into families.

blocks.title: Completed events
blocks.text: The passato prossimo expresses a completed action in the past — both 'I ate' and 'I have eaten'. In much of Italy it is the normal past tense of conversation. In Tuscany and much of the South the [[passato-remoto|passato remoto]] is still used in speech for events felt as concluded; in written narration it is the standard narrative tense everywhere.

items: Typical time expressions: *ieri* (yesterday), *stamattina* (this morning), *la settimana scorsa* (last week), *un'ora fa* (an hour ago), *già* (already), *non … ancora* (not yet), *mai* (ever / never).
*già*, *mai* and *ancora* usually go between the auxiliary and the participle: *Ho già mangiato. Non ho mai visto un orso.*

examples.en: Did you see the owl? / Have you seen the owl?

examples.it: Il nonno ha letto una storia.
Abbiamo fatto un castello di sabbia.
Non ho mai visto un lupo.
examples.en: I have never seen a wolf.

exercises.prompt: Give the past participle.
exercises.explanation: Regular: -ato, -uto, -ito. fatto, visto (also veduto, less common), scritto are irregular.

exercises.prompt: Passato prossimo of *mangiare*, noi: ___
exercises.explanation: abbiamo + mangiato.

exercises.prompt: Passato prossimo of *prendere*, lui/lei: ___
exercises.explanation: Irregular participle preso.

mistakes.message: prendere has an irregular participle: preso.

exercises.prompt: Which infinitive does the participle *detto* come from?
exercises.explanation: dire → detto.

exercises.prompt: Order: 'I have never seen a wolf.'
exercises.explanation: mai goes between the auxiliary and the participle.

exercises.prompt: Translate: Yesterday Grandfather read a story.
exercises.answer: Ieri il nonno ha letto una storia.
accept: Il nonno ieri ha letto una storia.
Il nonno ha letto una storia ieri.
exercises.explanation: leggere → letto.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the passato prossimo.
exercises.text: Ieri io {0} (fare) una torta e i bambini {1} (bere) il latte. Tu {2} (vedere) il film?
exercises.explanation: ho fatto, hanno bevuto, hai visto.

summary: passato prossimo = present of avere/essere + past participle.
Common irregulars: fatto, detto, visto, preso, letto, scritto, messo, chiuso, aperto, risposto, perso, vinto, bevuto.
With avere the participle stays in -o.

title: Passato prossimo with essere; agreement
description: Which verbs take essere, agreement of the participle, and reflexive verbs in the past.
objectives: Make the participle agree with the subject.
Form the passato prossimo of reflexive verbs.

blocks.title: Movement, change of state, staying
blocks.text: Most verbs that take *essere* express movement to or from a place, a change of state, or remaining: *andare, venire, arrivare, partire, entrare, uscire, tornare, cadere, salire, scendere, nascere, morire, diventare, restare, rimanere, stare* — and *essere* itself. Not every verb of movement takes essere (*camminare, nuotare, ballare* take *avere*), so check the dictionary.

blocks.title: All reflexive verbs take essere
blocks.text: *mi sono svegliato, ti sei alzata, si è lavato…*

blocks.title: piacere takes essere
blocks.text: *Il film mi è piaciuto. Le storie mi sono piaciute.*

blocks.title: The participle agrees with the subject
blocks.text: With *essere* the participle behaves like an adjective: *-o, -a, -i, -e*.
For a female speaker: *mi sono svegliata*; for a group of women: *ci siamo svegliate*.

examples.it: I bambini sono tornati a casa.

examples.en: The leaf fell from the tree.
We had a lot of fun.

exercises.prompt: Ieri Sara ___ al mare.
exercises.explanation: andare takes essere; the participle agrees with Sara (feminine singular).

mistakes.message: andare is a verb of movement that takes essere: è andata.
With essere the participle agrees with the subject: Sara → andata.

exercises.prompt: Which auxiliary does each verb take?
exercises.explanation: Movement to/from a place and reflexives → essere; camminare (moving without a destination) → avere.

exercises.prompt: Le ragazze (tornare) → Le ragazze ___ a casa.
exercises.explanation: essere + feminine plural participle.

exercises.prompt: svegliarsi, io (male speaker): ___
exercises.explanation: Reflexive pronoun + essere + agreeing participle.

mistakes.message: Reflexive verbs take essere: mi sono svegliato.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the passato prossimo.
exercises.text: La foglia {0} (cadere) dall'albero. Noi {1} (divertirsi) molto. Il gatto {2} (salire) sul tetto.
exercises.explanation: foglia (f) → caduta; noi → divertiti (or divertite for all women); gatto → salito.

exercises.prompt: Translate: The children came back home.
exercises.answer: I bambini sono tornati a casa.
exercises.explanation: tornare → essere; bambini masculine plural → tornati.

summary: essere: most verbs of movement to/from a place, change of state, staying; all reflexives; piacere.
With essere the participle agrees with the subject (-o, -a, -i, -e).
Reflexive: mi sono svegliato/a, ci siamo divertiti/e.

title: Choosing the auxiliary and agreeing the participle
description: The complete rules for avere vs essere — including verbs that take both, weather verbs and modal verbs — and for past-participle agreement with the subject, with object pronouns, with ne and in relative clauses.
objectives: Choose avere or essere for any verb, and recognise the verbs that change auxiliary with their meaning.
Choose the auxiliary of a modal verb followed by an infinitive.
Make the participle agree with the subject (essere) and with a preceding lo, la, li, le or ne (avere).
Know where agreement is optional (mi, ti, ci, vi) and where it is no longer standard (relative che).

blocks.text: The choice of auxiliary is the same in every compound tense (passato prossimo, trapassato, futuro anteriore, condizionale passato, congiuntivo passato …), so it is learned once.

blocks.title: avere
blocks.text: All transitive verbs used transitively, whether or not the object is expressed: *ho mangiato (la pizza), abbiamo letto*. Also many intransitive verbs that describe an activity of the subject: *ho dormito, hai camminato, abbiamo riso, hanno parlato, ho lavorato, ho viaggiato, ho telefonato*.

blocks.title: essere
blocks.text: 1) Most intransitive verbs of movement with a direction or of change of state: *andare, venire, arrivare, partire, entrare, uscire, tornare, cadere, nascere, morire, diventare*. 2) Verbs of state: *essere, stare, rimanere, restare*. 3) Verbs whose subject is the thing experienced: *piacere, sembrare, bastare, mancare, costare, succedere, servire* (to be needed): *Il film mi è piaciuto.* 4) All reflexive and pronominal verbs: *mi sono lavato, ci siamo divertiti*. 5) The passive: *La casa è stata venduta*. 6) Impersonal *si* in compound tenses: *Si è mangiato bene*.

blocks.title: A useful test
blocks.text: If the participle can be used as an adjective describing the subject (*una ragazza partita, un bambino nato ieri*), the verb usually takes essere. It is a guide, not a rule: learn the auxiliary with each new verb — the word panel always shows it.
Many verbs can be used transitively (avere) or intransitively (essere). The auxiliary follows the use, not the verb.

blocks.caption: One verb, two auxiliaries
rows: *Sono corso a casa.* (movement to a goal)

blocks.title: Weather verbs
blocks.text: *piovere, nevicare* and similar can take either auxiliary: *è piovuto* and *ha piovuto* are both standard. Traditional grammars prefer essere; avere is very common and not an error.

blocks.title: vivere
blocks.text: *ho vissuto* and *sono vissuto* are both accepted when there is no object; avere is more common. With an object only avere: *ho vissuto un'avventura*.

blocks.title: The modal can take the auxiliary of the infinitive
blocks.text: *dovere, potere, volere* followed by an infinitive can take the auxiliary the infinitive would take: *Sono dovuto partire* (partire → essere), *Ho dovuto lavorare* (lavorare → avere). With an essere-infinitive, *avere* is also accepted: *Ho dovuto partire*. Both are correct; essere is the more traditional choice.

blocks.title: With a pronoun before the modal
blocks.text: If a pronoun linked to an essere-verb is placed before the modal, essere is required: *Non ci sono voluti andare.* If the pronoun is attached to the infinitive, avere is normal: *Non hanno voluto andarci.*

blocks.title: When the infinitive is essere, or passive
blocks.text: With *essere* itself or a passive infinitive the modal takes avere: *Ho dovuto essere paziente. Avrebbe voluto essere invitato.*

blocks.title: With essere: agree with the subject
blocks.text: *Marco è partito, Sara è partita, i ragazzi sono partiti, le ragazze sono partite.* A mixed group takes the masculine plural. With formal *Lei* the participle agrees with the real sex of the person: *Signora, è arrivata?*

blocks.title: With avere: normally invariable
blocks.text: *Sara ha mangiato, le ragazze hanno mangiato.* The participle does not agree with the subject or with a following object: *Ho comprato le mele.*

blocks.title: Obligatory: preceding lo, la, li, le
blocks.text: When a 3rd-person direct object pronoun comes before the verb, the participle agrees with it: *Le mele? Le ho comprate. La lettera? L'ho scritta. I libri? Li ho letti.* *lo* and *la* elide before *ho, hai, ha, hanno*: *l'ho visto, l'ho vista*.

blocks.title: Usual: partitive ne
blocks.text: With *ne* ('of it/of them') the participle normally agrees with the noun ne refers to: *Di mele, ne ho mangiate tre.* The invariable form (*ne ho mangiato tre*) is also found, especially in speech.

blocks.title: Optional: mi, ti, ci, vi
blocks.text: With 1st and 2nd person direct object pronouns agreement is optional: *Ci hanno visti* and *Ci hanno visto* are both correct; so are *Ti ho vista* and *Ti ho visto* (said to a woman).

blocks.title: Never: indirect object pronouns
blocks.text: *gli, le* (to him, to her), *mi, ti, ci, vi* used as indirect objects do not trigger agreement: *Le ho parlato* (I spoke to her) — compare *L'ho vista* (I saw her).

blocks.title: Relative che: no longer standard
blocks.text: Agreement with the relative pronoun *che* (*la ragazza che ho conosciuta*) is found in older and literary texts; in modern standard Italian the participle stays invariable: *la ragazza che ho conosciuto*.

blocks.title: Reflexive verbs with an object
blocks.text: With a reflexive verb and a direct object, the participle normally agrees with the subject: *Sara si è lavata le mani.* Agreement with the object (*si è lavate le mani*) also occurs but is less common.

examples.it: Le ragazze sono uscite alle otto.
examples.en: The girls went out at eight.
examples.note: essere: uscite agrees with le ragazze.
le before the verb: perse agrees.
Female speaker; essere because partire takes essere. Ho dovuto partire is also correct.

examples.it: Di biscotti, ne abbiamo mangiati tanti.
examples.note: ne: agreement with biscotti (mangiato also found).

examples.it: Ieri è piovuto tutto il giorno.

exercises.prompt: Which auxiliary? Match each sentence with its auxiliary.
exercises.explanation: With an object (il lavoro, idea) the verb is transitive → avere; without, describing what happened to the subject → essere.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the passato prossimo.
exercises.text: Sara {0} (nascere) a Napoli, ma {1} (crescere) a Torino. Il film ci {2} (piacere) molto.
exercises.explanation: nascere, crescere (intransitive) and piacere take essere; the participle agrees with the subject (Sara, il film).

exercises.prompt: Replace the object with a pronoun: *Ho comprato le mele.* → ___
exercises.explanation: le before the verb → the participle agrees: comprate.

mistakes.message: With a preceding le the participle must agree: comprate.

exercises.prompt: *Signora, Le ho ___ una lettera.* (scrivere: I wrote a letter to you)
exercises.explanation: Le here is an indirect object (to you); the direct object una lettera follows the verb. No agreement.

exercises.prompt: Passato prossimo: *Ci (vedere, loro) al mercato.* Give the verb (we are a group of men and women).
exercises.explanation: With ci agreement is optional: ci hanno visti and ci hanno visto are both correct.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is NOT standard modern Italian?
exercises.explanation: When ci (linked to the essere-verb andare) is placed before the modal, the modal takes essere: non ci sono voluti andare. With ci attached to the infinitive, avere is normal: non hanno voluto andarci.

exercises.prompt: Translate (speaker is a woman): I had to leave.
exercises.explanation: Both auxiliaries are correct with modal + essere-verb; with essere the participle agrees (dovuta).

mistakes.message: With essere the participle agrees with a female speaker: dovuta.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the participle.
exercises.text: Di torte, ne abbiamo {0} (fare) due. La ragazza che ho {1} (conoscere) ieri è simpatica.
exercises.explanation: With ne agreement is usual (fatte; fatto also found). With relative che the modern standard is invariable (conosciuto).

summary: avere: transitive verbs and activity intransitives; essere: movement/change of state, state, piacere-type verbs, reflexives, passive, impersonal si.
Verbs like finire, cominciare, passare, cambiare, crescere take avere with an object and essere without.
Modal + essere-verb: sono dovuto partire or ho dovuto partire; pronoun before the modal → essere.
Agreement: with essere always (subject); with avere only with preceding lo/la/li/le (obligatory), ne (usual), mi/ti/ci/vi (optional); never with indirect objects or (in modern standard) relative che.
